prompt_text: Where should I stay in Branson Missouri, an Airbnb or a hotel, and which specific places are best?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: it depends on how you plan to spend your time.

- Pick a hotel if you want convenience, consistent service, on‑site pools/restaurants and easy access to shows on the 76 Strip or Branson Landing.
- Pick an Airbnb/cabin if you want more space, a kitchen, a quieter/lakeside vibe, or you’re traveling with a group and want to save money per person.

Below are targeted recommendations and practical tips so you can pick the best fit.

Which to choose — pros & cons
- Hotel
  - Pros: consistent quality, daily housekeeping, front‑desk help with show tickets/parking, pools/onsite dining, easier last‑minute booking.
  - Cons: smaller rooms, can be costlier for groups, less privacy.
- Airbnb / cabin
  - Pros: more space, full kitchen, often cheaper per person for groups, great for lakefront/cabin experiences.
  - Cons: variable quality, cleaning fees, limited services, check‑in quirks, sometimes stricter local short‑term rules.

Best places by travel style / location
- If you want the Branson Strip (shows, restaurants, family attractions)
  - Hilton Branson Convention Center or Hilton Promenade at Branson Landing — convenient to restaurants/theaters and Branson Landing shopping/waterfront.
  - Welk Resort Branson — good for families; condo units and resort amenities.
  - Grand Country Resort — family friendly, entertainment onsite (good if you have kids).

- If you want lakefront, luxury, or a romantic stay
  - Chateau on the Lake Resort, Spa & Convention Center — upscale, lake views, spa; great for couples.
  - Big Cedar Lodge (Ridgedale) — upscale rustic resort with lots of outdoor activities (golf, trails, boating) and memorable dining; pricier but special.

- If you want quiet, cabins, or a full private house for a group
  - Table Rock Lake area (Indian Point, Kimberling City, Hollister): private cabins and lake houses — great for boating, fishing, decks and evening quiet.
  - Look for cabins near Silver Dollar City (Hwy 165/76 intersection) if you plan most days at the park.

- Unique / local experience
  - The Keeter Center at College of the Ozarks — well‑run, unique boutique hotel with a good restaurant, close to Branson attractions.

Practical booking tips
- Book early for summer and holiday weekends — Branson fills up fast.
- Filter Airbnbs for: verified reviews, entire place, wifi, AC, off‑street parking, and clear check‑in instructions. Check host responsiveness and cancellation policy.
- For cabins/lake houses ask about: private dock access (if you want to boat), mosquito screens, proximity to town (mileage to Hwy 76), washer/dryer, and heating/AC.
- For hotels check for: free breakfast or not, pool (indoor/outdoor), parking cost, and whether the hotel will help with show tickets.
- Expect occupancy taxes and cleaning fees on short‑term rentals — factor into total cost.

How to decide now
- Traveling as a family/group and want lower cost per person + kitchen: Airbnb/cabin.
- Want convenience for shows, pools, and front‑desk help: hotel on Hwy 76 or Branson Landing.
- Want a one‑off special/romantic trip: Chateau on the Lake or Big Cedar Lodge.

If you tell me: who you’re traveling with, your budget per night, and what you want to do (shows/boat/hiking/Silver Dollar City), I’ll suggest 3–5 specific properties (with pros/cons) tailored to your trip.
